slides.title: Pim's notebook of tricksters
slides.text: Some tricks are not accidents. Behind each one is a threat actor: a person or group trying to get something they should not have.
slides.alt: A Pro trick card: the sender name looks friendly, but a faked name is exactly what spoofing means.

slides.title: Four kinds of actor
slides.text: Meet the gallery in plain words: the scammer wants money, the account thief wants in, the vandal wants damage, and the spy wants secrets. None of them is glamorous. Each is simply trying to take what is not theirs.
slides.alt: A parcel trick: a delivery you never ordered is waiting, and a small fee must be paid within two hours.

slides.title: Name the want, pick the guard
slides.text: A fake message from the school office asks for account details. Work out who is behind it before you act.
steps: Guard: do not reply; report it
slides.alt: A Pro trick card: the sender name looks friendly, but a faked name is exactly what spoofing means.

slides.title: Permission is the whole difference
slides.text: Testing a network's locks can be ethical or malicious, and permission is the whole difference. With permission it is defense work. Without it, it is breaking in, whatever the reason given.
slides.alt: Share or Shield: your mailbox key. Anyone who has it can read your post and send as you, so it stays private.

slides.title: Not like the films
slides.text: Films dress hacking up as instant magic, which is a costume too. Real defense is slow, careful and lawful, and it is a real job people are paid to do well.
slides.alt: Design the rule set: three things go wrong on this road, and four rule cards are there to catch them.

words.means: a person or group behind an attack or trick
the thing someone wants, which drives what they do
doing what is right, including asking permission first
being allowed, clearly, by the person in charge

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Would You Rather, choose the Online topic, and play Online: share or keep. Then replay Packet Post at Spot the Trick on Pro, and name the actor behind each trick.
slides.alt: An online dilemma in Pro: make it public and be found, or keep it private and stay safe — a real tradeoff.
